title: 100 Wikidays on French Wikipedia : How I decided to promote scientists
content:
From July 30 to November 6, 2026 (a total of 100 consecutive days) I created at least one article on the french Wikipedia. My initial objective was to keep the Beninese Wikimedians, my first community, active.

On July 30, I started by creating an article about the renowned expert Raïmi Amadou. Afterward, I encouraged Beninese Wikimedians to join me. So, I created event, 100 Wikidays des Wikimédiens du Bénin on Meta.

And here we go, 100 days at our own pace. I have to set a good example, since charity begins at home.
So, I continued to create articles day by day. But I was confronted with the absence of many world-renowned scientists on the French Wikipedia and often on the english Wikipedia as well. Yet they are eligible under specific criteria for having received ACFAS awards or a medal from the National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS).

So, I decided to identify the recipients of these awards, find sources on their careers, and locate their scientific articles. Once I had gathered the sources, I moved on to creating Wikipedia articles about these scientists, who are European or Canadian.

title: Wiki Indaba 2026: Beyond the Conference, Building Connections Across Africa
content:
From 13 to 15 November 2026, I had the opportunity to participate in Wiki Indaba 2026 in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire. The conference brought together Wikimedians from across Africa and beyond to exchange experiences, discuss common challenges, and explore new opportunities for collaboration.

This year’s theme, “Africa’s Future: Knowledge Equity and Innovation,” reflected an important question for our movement: how can we ensure that African knowledge, languages, cultures, and perspectives are better represented and accessible through Wikimedia projects?

For me, Wiki Indaba was not simply about attending sessions. It was an opportunity to connect with contributors working in different environments, understand their approaches, and reflect on how we can improve our own work.

One of the most interesting aspects of Wiki Indaba was the diversity of experiences represented.

African Wikimedia communities operate in different linguistic, cultural, and technological contexts. Some focus on developing local-language Wikipedias, others on documenting cultural heritage, improving access to reliable sources, or introducing new contributors to Wikimedia projects.

title: I Walked Into My Own College Hall and Told Everyone Where I Started
content:
My first open source contribution felt tiny when it happened. Nobody clapped. A patch got merged somewhere on the internet, and my laptop was the only witness.

On 21st August, I stood in front of a hall full of students at United Institute Of Technology Prayagraj and told them exactly that. The first slide on the screen said “Where I started”, and honestly, I think it was the most important slide of the whole day. What I didn’t fully admit to myself then was that this was also the last event I’d be running as Core Team of WikiClub Tech UIT 2025-2026.

Open Source Day was organized by WikiClub Tech UIT together with GDG Prayagraj. The idea was simple. Most students think open source is a club for geniuses who write kernel code at 3 am. We wanted to show them it’s a door you can walk through, even if you’ve never touched Git in your life. The day started at 10 am with the welcome of our dignitaries. Then the sessions began, and I’ll admit I was more nervous than I let on.

title: Celebrating 14 Years of Wikidata: Learning, Creativity and Community Engagement in the Igbo Wikimedians User Group
content:
Wikidata’s 14th birthday celebration in the Igbo Wikimedians User Group began virtually on Friday, 16 October 2026, for our community members who are neither in Abuja nor Awka. The virtual celebration was fun as we reflected on our success, challenges, and the way forward. The highlight of the session was when community members’ knowledge of Wikidata and its sister projects was tested.

Following the virtual celebration, we gathered in-person at two locations: Godwin Art Gallery, Awka, Anambra State, and the Enspirehub, Merit House, Maitama, Abuja. The celebration brought together 55 participants for a day of learning, creativity, games, networking, and appreciation of the free knowledge movement. The event provided an opportunity for participants to explore Wikidata, understand its importance, and experience knowledge-sharing in a fun and interactive environment. It was facilitated by Senator Choko, Macocobovi, and King ChristLike.

title: Connecting Communities and Sharing Knowledge: My Experience at Wiki Indaba 2026 in Abidjan
content:
From 13 to 15 November 2026, I had the opportunity to participate in the Wiki Indaba 2026 conference in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire. The conference brought together Wikimedians, language activists, open knowledge advocates, and representatives of Wikimedia communities from across Africa to share experiences, discuss challenges, and explore opportunities for strengthening the movement on the continent.

Representing the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group, I was particularly excited to meet fellow Wikimedians, learn from their experiences, and explore ideas that could contribute to the growth of our community and other Mabia language projects.

Our presentation highlighted the importance of protecting indigenous languages in the digital space and how Wikimedia projects provide opportunities to document, preserve, and promote the Dagbani language and cultural heritage.

We also shared the work, experiences, and achievements of the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group, including our efforts to make Dagbani knowledge accessible to a global audience.

title: NJA College Wiki Club Holds Maiden Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons Training Workshop
content: On Saturday, 14 November 2026, the NJA College of Education Wiki Club successfully organised its maiden physical Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons training workshop on campus. The workshop was organised by the Wali Wikimedians Community in direct collaboration with the Students’ Representative Council (SRC) of NJA College of Education. The event marked an important milestone in the club’s activities, as it provided the first opportunity for members and interested students to receive practical training in contributing to Wikimedia projects through a physical workshop.
